    model segregates the biomass into individual sludge flocs implying all floc properties (e.g. size) to be segregated too. This results in property distributions instead of a single quantity for a certain property. Models describing the time evolution of these property distributions are known as Population Balance Models (PBM). The general format of a one-dimensional PBM (i.e. with one property) looks like (Ramkrishna, 2000):
(1) \frac{\partial n(x,t)}{\partial t}+\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\dot{X}(x,t)n(x,t)\right)=h(x,t)_{agg}+h(x,t)_{break}    [code: PDE, computes ?, code proposes balance]
    where for this application x is the floc size (expressed as volume), n(x,t) the floc size distribution function (#.cm⁻³) (expressed in numbers), $ \dot{X}(x,t) $ the growth rate (s⁻¹) and h(x,t)gg/break the net aggregation/breakage rates (cm⁻³.s⁻¹). Hence, eq. 1 describes the time evolution of the floc size distribution. Since the model will be used to describe rather short flocculation experiments (max. 4h), it can be assumed that no significant growth occurs ( $ \dot{X}(x,t)=0 $). h(x,t)gg/break account for discontinuous aggregation and breakage processes (Figure 1).     Aggregation models are often based on the Smoluchowski model (Ramkrishna, 2000):
(2) \begin{aligned}h(x,t)_{agg}=&\frac{1}{2}\int\limits_{0}^{x}\alpha\beta(x-x^{\prime},x^{\prime})n(x-x^{\prime},t)n(x^{\prime},t)dx\\&-n(x,t)\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}\alpha\beta(x,x^{\prime})n(x^{\prime},t)dx\end{aligned}    [code: algebraic, computes ?, code proposes constitutive]
    where $\alpha$ (-) is the collision efficiency and $\beta(x-x',x)$ (cm$^3$.s$^{-1}$) the collision frequency for particles of volume $x$ (cm$^3$) and $x-x'$ (cm$^3$). This model describes both the transport of flocs towards one another ($\beta$) and the probability that these collisions lead to aggregation ($\alpha$) accounting for short-range forces like van der Waals and hydrodynamic interactions. The description of $\beta(x-x',x$) used in this study was taken from Spicer & Pratsinis (1996):
(3) \beta(x-x^{\prime},x)=0.31\overline{G}\left(x^{\prime/3}+(x-x^{\prime})^{\prime/3}\right)^{3}    [code: algebraic, computes \beta, code proposes constitutive]
    in which:
(4) \overline{G}=\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\nu}}    [code: algebraic, computes \overline{G}, code proposes constitutive]

Breakage models typically look like (Ramkrishna, 2000):

    where S(x) is the breakage rate of particles of size x (s $ ^{-1} $) and $ \Gamma $ the breakage distribution function. S(x) was taken from Spicer & Pratsinis (1996):
(6) S(x)=Ax^{a}    [code: algebraic, computes S, code proposes constitutive]
    where a is a constant (=1/3) and A the breakage rate coefficient (cm⁻³s⁻¹). When binary breakage is assumed, which was the case in this study, Γ equals 2.

Kumar & Ramkrishna (1996) compared this fixed pivot technique with an analytical solution for a simple PBM and found that it suffers from overpredictions of numbers when large gradients are present in the distribution. To deal with this, they introduced the moving pivot, and showed that this technique gave a much better prediction of the analytical solution, even for a coarse grid. To confirm this improved accuracy in this study, the PBM was solved with both techniques for $ \alpha=0.0065 $ and A=201.5. The simulation results in Figure 2 are represented as cumulative oversize numbers (CON)
(9) C O N ( x, t ) = \int _ { x } ^ { \infty } n ( x ^ { \prime }, t )   d x ^ { \prime }    [code: algebraic, computes CON, code proposes constitutive]
    in order to emphasise the predictions of the large floc size range and the $0^{\mathrm{th}}$ moment of the distribution in one single plot. Symbols:
  n: Floc size distribution function [#.cm⁻³] (computed)
  x: Floc size, expressed as volume [cm³] (computed)
  \dot{X}: Growth rate [s⁻¹] (computed)
  h: Net aggregation/breakage rates [cm⁻³.s⁻¹] (computed)
  a: Exponent in the breakage-rate size law [-] (computed)
  g: Mean velocity gradient in the aggregation kernel [s⁻¹] (computed)
  break: Breakage contribution to the net population-balance rate [cm⁻³.s⁻¹] (computed)
  \alpha: Collision efficiency [-] (parameter)
  \beta: Collision frequency for particles of volume x and x-x′ [cm³.s⁻¹] (computed)
  x^{\prime}: Integration variable representing floc volume [cm³] (variable)
  d: Differential element of the particle-size coordinate in the integrals. (variable)
  \overline{G}: Average velocity gradient. [s^{-1}] (computed)
  \varepsilon: Average turbulent energy dissipation rate. [m^2.s^{-3}] (variable)
  \nu: Kinematic viscosity. [m^2.s^{-1}] (parameter)
  S: Breakage rate of particles of size x. [s^{-1}] (computed)
  \Gamma: Breakage distribution function. (parameter)
  A: Coefficient in the particle breakage-rate law S(x)=Ax^a. (parameter)
  D: Mass mean diameter, D[4,3]. (computed)
  [4,3]: Moment-order indices indicating the fourth-to-third-moment ratio used to calculate D[4,3]. [-] (computed)
  \Delta F_{N}: Increment in the number-based particle-size distribution used in the moment sums. (variable)
  x_{i}: diameter of size class i [μm] (variable)
  CON: cumulative oversize numbers (computed)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - No significant growth occurs during the short flocculation experiments.
  - Binary breakage is assumed, so Γ equals 2.

laws.description: Tracks the floc-size distribution over time through size-space growth and aggregation and breakage source terms.
laws.quote: Hence, eq. 1 describes the time evolution of the floc size distribution.
laws.law_type_reason: It balances accumulation and transport in size space against aggregation and breakage contributions.
laws.issue: The stated unit of \dot{X} is s⁻¹, but because x is a volume, the size-space transport term requires \dot{X} to have units of volume per time.

laws.description: Computes the net aggregation contribution from floc formation by collisions and loss of flocs through aggregation.
laws.quote: This model describes both the transport of flocs towards one another (β) and the probability that these collisions lead to aggregation (α) accounting for short-range forces like van der Waals and hydrodynamic interactions.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the collision-based aggregation rate that a rival model could replace.

assumptions.text: The collision efficiency is chosen to be constant between 0 and 1.
assumptions.quote: α was chosen to be a constant between 0 and 1.

laws.issue: The first integral is over x′ but is printed with differential dx; it should be dx′.

laws.description: Calculates the collision frequency between flocs from their volumes and the average velocity gradient.
laws.law_type_reason: It provides a collision-frequency correlation for the aggregation model.
laws.issue: The exponent on (x−x′) is printed as ′/3; it should be 1/3 to match the other volume term and give the stated collision-frequency units.

laws.description: Calculates the average velocity gradient from turbulent energy dissipation and kinematic viscosity.
laws.law_type_reason: It is a correlation for a physical property used by the collision-frequency law.
laws.issue: The equation uses ε without an overbar, whereas the text identifies the quantity in this correlation as average turbulent energy dissipation rate ε̄.

laws.description: Computes the net breakage contribution by adding fragments from larger flocs and subtracting flocs that break at size x.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the breakage gain and loss terms rather than a conservation balance for a fixed species.
laws.issue: The loss term includes Γ(x,x′), leaving x′ unintegrated; the parent-loss term should remove flocs at rate n(x,t)S(x) without the daughter-size distribution.

laws.description: Calculates the breakage rate as a size-dependent power law.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the size dependence of the particle breakage rate.

assumptions.text: The exponent a is fixed at 1/3.

laws.issue: With x expressed as volume and a=1/3, A must have units cm⁻¹s⁻¹ for S to have units s⁻¹, not the stated cm⁻³s⁻¹.

laws.description: Calculates the mass mean diameter as the ratio of the fourth and third moments of the number-based size distribution.
laws.quote: as the ratio of the fourth and third moment of the distribution:
laws.law_type_reason: It defines D[4,3] from weighted sums over the size classes.
laws.issue: The terms are printed as ΔF_N(x_i,x_i^4) and ΔF_N(x_i,x_i^3), but the text defines ΔF_N(x_i) as the number fraction; the moments require multiplying that fraction by x_i^4 and x_i^3, respectively.

laws.description: Calculates the cumulative number of flocs with size at least x at time t.
laws.quote: The simulation results in Figure 2 are represented as cumulative oversize numbers (CON)
laws.law_type_reason: It defines CON by integrating the size distribution above the specified size.
